analysis: Monday's open is a reset, not a continuation: the weekend reversed Friday's peace hopes, and the oil-to-yields-to-risk chain is back on. What changed vs Friday's briefs: (1) the 10Y has pushed back above 5.21% in overnight trade (5.214%, +4.9 bps) — just under Friday's 5.2297% 2007 intraday high — with markets now pricing a >70% chance of an October Fed hike; (2) the Iran story flipped from cautious optimism to a confirmed rejection — Trump called Tehran's 7-day Hormuz/ceasefire offer 'unacceptable' on Saturday; the WSJ add that he expects to resume bombing after the midterms is single-source but deepens the bid-under-oil; (3) NVDA has a new single-source demand headline (The Information: Beijing may approve ByteDance/Alibaba RTX Pro 5500 purchases, ~1M units under discussion) — NVDA faded the initial overnight bounce, so the tape wants confirmation before repricing; (4) semis/optical/crypto are all red premarket (SNDK -3.35%, INTC -3.16%, COHR -3.15%, MU -2.15%), and tech leads the futures slide (NQ -0.9% vs S&P -0.4%). Counterweight carried forward: Friday closed positive (S&P +0.51% to 7,743.41, VIX down to 14.87), Meta's week still +13% despite Friday's -3.33%, and the AI-demand bid keeps confirming from hard sources (Musk's xAI 220k GB300 post, AKAM's Anthropic deal). The MarketWatch breadth note deserves attention: only ~51% of S&P constituents sit above their 200-day vs 73% at the July 28 low — narrow leadership while the index flirts with records. Signal vs noise: futures, yields, oil moves, the Trump rejection, MSFT Copilot revamp, Tesla's two-event week, and MU's Sept 30 earnings date are confirmed; the NVDA/China approval terms and any Hormuz roadmap remain single-source/unconfirmed — fragile. A/D ratio and volume vs 20-day remain unavailable from sourced pages.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures are pointing to a lower open Monday: Nasdaq-100 -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.4%, Dow -0.3%. The trigger is geopolitical — Trump rejected Iran's 7-day ceasefire/Hormuz reopening offer over the weekend, calling it 'unacceptable' Saturday on Fox News, with no breakthrough in talks. Asian chip stocks dragged Japan and South Korea; Europe's tech-light Stoxx 600 was +0.3%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Friday's late-day bounce was priced on peace hopes; those hopes just died, so the reversal risk flags in Friday's briefs materialized — the open resets to risk-off with oil and yields as the drivers.

headlines.headline: Oil and yields are both climbing Monday: Brent +2.4% to $106.82, WTI +2.3% to $94.55; the 10Y is up 4.9 bps to 5.214% (fresh multi-year high, just under Friday's 5.2297% 2007 intraday print), the 30Y at 5.518%, the 2Y at 4.920%. Markets now price a >70% chance of an October Fed quarter-point hike. Gold fell 1.9% to ~$4,200 and bitcoin slipped below $83k on the rate-repricing. WSJ also reported Trump told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms.
headlines.why_it_matters: The 'one factor world' chain — oil driving rates, rates driving all asset classes — is back: a resumption-of-war headline puts a bid under both the inflation trade and the rate-hike trade, which is the exact squeeze that kills equity multiples.

headlines.headline: The Information reported Sunday that China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology asked ByteDance and Alibaba to submit purchase plans for Nvidia's new RTX Pro 5500 (a Blackwell workstation GPU with 84GB GDDR7, priced above $6,000) — and told some firms the purchases could be approved. ByteDance is reportedly weighing ~1M units. NVDA shares initially rose in overnight trade then reversed to -0.4%; NVDA closed Friday at $225.07. The ministry has not publicly confirmed approvals, and timing/quantity are unresolved.
headlines.why_it_matters: A potential reopening of China demand for NVDA would be a real revenue datapoint, but it rests on one outlet's report with no official confirmation — and the overnight fade shows the tape agrees, so treat as fragile until confirmed.

headlines.headline: Tesla has a two-event week: the long-delayed Roadster reveal happens Thursday Oct 1 in Waco, Texas (reveal only — production is a year-plus out; reservations reopened Sept 18 at a $50k deposit), followed by Q3 deliveries on Friday Oct 2. Consensus is ~454,000 vehicles, but estimates span 435k (Goldman) to ~480k (Kalshi) — an unusually wide range. Tesla teased a new Roadster light bar at Thursday's Semi event. Starship Flight 14 is also set for Monday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Back-to-back catalysts into a stock pinned near its 50-day (~$350): the delivery consensus spread shows unusual uncertainty, so Friday's print has real move potential, and the Roadster reveal sets the sentiment tone the day before.

headlines.headline: Microsoft unveiled a major Copilot overhaul Friday (Reuters): a 'super app' with Code (natural-language app building via GitHub Copilot tech), an always-on Autopilot agent with its own corporate identity, and Word/Excel/PowerPoint embedded directly in Copilot. MSFT led the Mag7 on Friday at +3.66%; Oppenheimer raised its target to $570 on the enterprise-AI-agent shift.
headlines.why_it_matters: The enterprise AI-agent pivot gives MSFT a usage-based monetization path off its M365/Azure distribution — the product news behind Friday's Mag7 leadership, and a counterweight to today's macro tape.

headlines.headline: Michael Burry disclosed expanded short positions in Micron (MU), Nebius (NBIS), and Palantir (PLTR), extending his bearish AI thesis (he already holds Nvidia and Tesla shorts) and reiterating a warning of a possible '1987-type fall' in AI-linked stocks, per Stocktwits. MU was -2.15% premarket alongside a weak memory/storage tape (SNDK -3.35%, WDC -2.52%); Micron reports earnings Sept 30.
headlines.why_it_matters: High-profile bearish positioning two days before the sector's read-through earnings: if MU's print is strong, it directly tests the shorts; a weak one validates the memory-pricing fears Burry is trading on.

usac.headline: Wall Street Zen downgraded USAC to Hold (from Buy) in a note issued Saturday; on Friday, units broke below their 200-day moving average, closing at $25.4880 vs the $27.12 200-day line. Four trading days remain before the NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer (NYSE ends Oct 2, TXSE begins Oct 5, ticker unchanged).
usac.why_it_matters: Technical breakdown plus a weekend downgrade right before the listing move — carried fundamentals are unchanged (Q2 revenue $342.1M, adj. EBITDA $193.2M, DCF coverage 1.65x, $0.525 distribution, FY EBITDA guidance $770-800M confirmed), and the unit price moves into the TXSE transition against a stronger oil tape (Brent +2.4%), a near-term sector tailwind.

watch_next: Wednesday: August PCE (consensus 3.7% headline / 3.3% core) — the next hard data point for the October Fed-hike repricing now >70% priced.
Friday: September jobs report (consensus +100k nonfarm, unemployment 4.1%) plus Tesla Q3 deliveries (consensus ~454k, wide range) — a double macro/company catalyst day.
Thursday: Tesla Roadster reveal (Waco, 5:30pm PT) — sentiment setup for Friday's delivery print.
Sept 30: Micron earnings — the memory/pricing read-through for MU, SNDK, WDC, STX into Burry's fresh short positioning.
Does the 10Y re-test Friday's 5.2297% intraday 2007 high, and any confirmation or denial of the Iran stalemate / NVDA-China approval stories.
